turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so let's not waste it. My son found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
Before we start, I reread Owen's last three essays this morning.
This morning. The zero went in a week ago, so you read his work after you'd already decided. Who decided, Hale?
He writes like someone who was read to every night. That was you, wasn't it?
Don't manage me. You still haven't answered who decided, and on what basis.
You've raised a genuinely thoughtful kid. I mean that.
Then why are we here, Hale? A thoughtful kid with a zero, and still no answer. Who entered it, and what was it based on?
Which is why I'd hate for this to become a fight between two people who obviously both care about him.
It became a fight when the zero went into the gradebook before anyone picked up a phone. I'm not here to care with you, I'm here for an answer. Withdraw the zero, or tell me what it rests on.
